A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, with moved and renumbered material identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on Heavy Grippers, Colors and Lights Out, including generalization accuracies and training curves in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds controlled generalization results separating object-count growth from plan-length growth in Figure 6 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The C*-RASP operations, formal learning procedure and experimental transformer architecture and objective remain unchanged. The expanded reciprocal-activation discussion concerns an assumption already present in v1 Appendix C.1.

E1.justification: The same three domains and six formulations remain. v2 adds controlled OOD scenarios for Colors and Heavy Grippers in which object count and plan length increase independently; v1's corresponding evaluations coupled their growth.

E2.justification: The comparison pairs remain well-formed versus delete-free Heavy Grippers, well-formed versus STRIPS Colors, and well-formed versus conditional-effects Lights Out. The new controlled evaluations reuse the existing pairs, and newly cited methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 6 and Table 4 introduce tests fixing plan length at 100 while varying object count, and tests fixing object count at 15 for Colors or 140 for Heavy Grippers while varying plan length. The original splits, training budgets, model settings and accuracy metric are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a targeted analysis testing generalization under separate object-count and plan-length shifts. New Appendix F provides worked Ferry and Satellite case studies supporting the existing discussion of semantic well-formedness. Earlier learning-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four seeds, disclose exclusion of one unsuccessful STRIPS Colors seed, and describe average accuracy, best-seed results and standard deviations for the original curves. v2 introduces no new run-count information or statistical uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 6 and Table 4 add controlled-condition accuracies: for example, with plan length 100 and 15 objects, Colors achieves 0.9954 for well-formed and 0.6663 for STRIPS. Appendix F newly presents Ferry as well-formed and Satellite as not well-formed. Original accuracy plots and the aggregate 70% well-formedness finding remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 repairs the conditional-effects proof using a direct equal-length homomorphism whose preimage is PARITY, removing the earlier kernel/intersection detour. Theorem 3.6 and its Appendix B restatement now explicitly specify C*-RASP[Pos]. These are localized corrections to existing results; the main learning theorem is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the growing-alphabet C*-RASP framework and the distinction between generalizable planning formulations and harder STRIPS or conditional-effects cases. The additional evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 5.3 and Remark C.1 more explicitly qualify the guarantees through idealized activations, translation invariance, exhaustive training-distribution matching and limited modeling of training dynamics. Section 5.2 also explains the role of ordered object identifiers and their potential connection to index hints.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly documents the manual procedure behind the earlier well-formedness assessment: examining ten IPC domains, checking action definitions and consulting problem generators, with a generator-source link. Existing model, tokenization, optimization, hardware and code-access details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Isik et al. (2025) and Kraus et al. (2026), positioning ordered-alphabet generalization relative to interchangeable embeddings and index hints. It also expands the comparison with Nunez-Molina et al. Bibliographic updates and consolidation of duplicate Plansformer references do not represent additional research changes.

P1.justification: Targeted rewriting expands the conditional-effects proof, related work, limitations and activation explanations, and adds Appendix F. The overall section order and narrative remain stable, alongside smaller wording, publication-header and bibliography edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a membership-summary table to a colored hierarchy diagram with an expanded caption. v2 adds the controlled-evaluation Figure 6 and Table 4. Existing benchmark and training plots are retained, with renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves rigor through a direct PARITY reduction that avoids the earlier problematic intermediate argument. The new controlled evaluations separate two previously coupled generalization factors, while clearer limitations and the documented manual assessment improve transparency. These are useful, targeted improvements to the existing contribution.
